evidence.note: The Muntahā and its sharḥ state decisively that the one freed by lot does not inherit, since the lot has no role in lineage.

evidence.excerpt_ar: واحدة للأطول منهما ما لم تكن حاملا. قاله في المغني، والشرح، والرعايتين،
evidence.note: For one wife divorced (unspecified, or specified then forgotten) before the husband died, al-Inṣāf says each wife observes the longer of the two ʿiddas, citing al-Mughnī, al-Sharḥ, al-Riʿāyatayn, al-Ḥāwī, al-Wajīz and others.

evidence.excerpt_ar: اعتددن) أي النساء التي طلق بعضهن ولم يعلم (بأطول الأجلين من عدة الوفاة
evidence.note: Kashshāf/Iqnāʿ: if the husband dies before the taʿyīn they all observe the longer term, which is al-Qāḍī's position.

evidence.excerpt_ar: نسائه سوى حامل الأطول منهما وإن ارتابت متوفى عنها زمن تربصها أو بعده
evidence.note: The Muntahā (the preceding words: "man ṭallaqa muʿayyana wa-nasiyahā aw mubhama thumma māta qabla qurʿa iʿtadda kull") makes every non-pregnant wife observe the longer term.

evidence.excerpt_ar: والوجه الثاني: هو نجس. قلت: وهو الصواب، لأن القرائن المحتفة بذلك تقتضي
evidence.note: In Taṣḥīḥ al-Furūʿ (masʾala 24) al-Mardāwī rules the water impure ('wa-huwa al-ṣawāb'), since the surrounding indications weaken the aṣl, matching position 0.

evidence.excerpt_ar: ولوغا كلب أدخل رأسه في إناء ثم بفيه رطوبة فلا ينجس وان أصابه ماء ميزاب
evidence.note: The Iqnāʿ states decisively that when one doubts whether a dog that put its head in a vessel with a wet mouth licked, the water is not rendered impure (position 1).

evidence.excerpt_ar: وفي بعض نسخ الفروع: وثم أي هناك - وجد (بفيه رطوبة فلا ينجس) ؛ لأن
evidence.note: Kashshāf follows the Iqnāʿ: not impure, because the aṣl is that no licking took place (position 1).

evidence.excerpt_ar: فلا ينجس لكن يكره ما ظنت نجاسته احتياطا.
evidence.note: Sharḥ al-Muntahā reads the Muntahā's general rule as covering this case: not impure, though what is thought impure is disliked as a precaution (position 1).

evidence.excerpt_ar: قلت: الصواب أنه طاهر لأنه الأصل، وهو ظاهر كلام جماعة، ثم وجدت شيخنا في
evidence.note: Under masʾala 25, after quoting Ibn Rajab's two wujūh, al-Mardāwī rules that the creature is pure because that is the aṣl ('al-ṣawāb'), i.e. position 1.

entries.note: Each riwāya is made the madhhab by a different author.

evidence.excerpt_ar: وأما طين الشوارع: فما ظنت نجاسته من ذلك: فهو طاهر على الصحيح من
evidence.note: al-Inṣāf rules that street mud thought to be impure is pure 'ʿalā al-ṣaḥīḥ min al-madhhab' (with al-Furūʿ giving it precedence), i.e. the mansūṣ riwāya of position 0.

evidence.excerpt_ar: (وطين الشارع وترابه طاهر) وإن ظنت نجاسته؛ لأن الأصل الطهارة (ما لم
evidence.note: The Iqnāʿ and Kashshāf state decisively that street mud is pure even when thought impure, because the aṣl is purity (position 0).

evidence.excerpt_ar: وطين شارع ظنت نجاسته طاهر. وكذا ترابه، عملا بالأصل. فإن تحققت نجاسته عفي
evidence.note: Sharḥ al-Muntahā also rules street mud thought impure to be pure by the aṣl, with only small amounts excused once its impurity is certain (position 0).

evidence.excerpt_ar: (جاز) التيمم بترابها وإن شك فيه، أو في نجاسة التراب الذي يتيمم به، جاز
evidence.note: Kashshāf rules that where it is doubted whether the cemetery was repeatedly exhumed, tayammum with its soil is valid because the aṣl is purity (citing al-Sharḥ), i.e. position 1.

evidence.excerpt_ar: في التكرار صح التيمم به، ولا بطين، لكن إن أمكنه تجفيفه، والتيمم به قبل
evidence.note: Sharḥ al-Muntahā: if one doubts whether exhumation was repeated, tayammum with the cemetery's soil is valid, so the soil is treated as pure (position 1).

evidence.excerpt_ar: الموتى ولحومهم. وإن شك في تكرر الدفن فيها، أو في نجاسة التراب الذي تيمم
evidence.note: al-Mughnī permits tayammum where repeated burial is doubted, because purity is the aṣl and is not removed by doubt (position 1).

entries.note: Riwāyas 1 and 2 agree that washing is not required.

evidence.excerpt_ar: هذا المذهب مطلقا. وعليه الجمهور. قال في مجمع البحرين: هذا أظهر
evidence.note: On the Muqniʿ's 'the clothes and vessels of unbelievers are pure and permitted to use unless their impurity is known', al-Inṣāf says this is the madhhab absolutely and that the majority hold it, i.e. riwāya 1 (permissibility).

evidence.excerpt_ar: تكره وثياب الكفار كلهم وأوانيهم طاهرة إن جهل حالها حتى ماولي عوراتهم كما
evidence.note: The Iqnāʿ rules that the clothes and vessels of all unbelievers are pure when their state is unknown, even what touched their private parts (position 0).

evidence.excerpt_ar: الأوثان (وأوانيهم) أي أواني الكفار كلهم (طاهرة إن جهل حالها، حتى ما ولي
evidence.note: Kashshāf extends this to Magians and idolaters as well: pure if their state is unknown, because the aṣl of purity is not removed by doubt (position 0).

evidence.excerpt_ar: مباح وتصح الصلاة في ثياب المرضعة والحائض والصبي مع الكراهة ما لم تعلم
evidence.note: The Iqnāʿ states decisively that prayer in a child's (or nursing or menstruating woman's) clothes is valid but disliked unless their impurity is known, i.e. karāha (position 0).

evidence.excerpt_ar: كمدمني الخمر؛ لأن الأصل طهارتها (مع الكراهة) احتياطا للعبادة.
evidence.note: Kashshāf: valid because their clothes are pure by the aṣl, but disliked as a precaution for the act of worship (position 0).

evidence.excerpt_ar: الثالثة: تصح الصلاة في ثياب المرضعة والحائض والصبي، مع الكراهة، قدمه
evidence.note: al-Inṣāf gives karāha as the position Majmaʿ al-Baḥrayn puts first, records a riwāya of no karāha, and notes that Ibn Abī Mūsā likened a child's garment to a Magian's (no prayer before washing).

evidence.excerpt_ar: قوله (وأما الشك، فمتى شك: في عدد الركعات بنى على اليقين) هذا المذهب
evidence.note: al-Inṣāf says building on certainty for anyone who doubts the number of rakʿas is the madhhab absolutely, and that the great majority of the aṣḥāb hold it (Abū Bakr, al-Qāḍī, Abū al-Khaṭṭāb, al-Majd and others), i.e. riwāya 1.

evidence.excerpt_ar: ويبني على اليقين من شك في ركن أو عدد ركعات ولا يرجع واحد إلى فعل إمامه
evidence.note: The Muntahā states without distinction that whoever doubts the number of rakʿas builds on certainty (position 0).

evidence.excerpt_ar: بقوله (من شك في عدد الركعات بنى على اليقين ولو) كان الشاك (إماما) روي عن
evidence.note: The Iqnāʿ and Kashshāf rule that one builds on certainty even when the one in doubt is the imam, which rejects riwāya 3's distinction (position 0).

evidence.excerpt_ar: لو شك في عدد الأشواط في نفس الطواف فالصحيح من المذهب: أنه لا يأخذ إلا
evidence.note: al-Inṣāf: on the soundest view of the madhhab, one who doubts the number of circuits during ṭawāf takes only the certain count (it is a naṣṣ, and al-Furūʿ gives it precedence), i.e. position 0.

evidence.excerpt_ar: (وإن شك في عدد الأشواط أخذ باليقين) ليخرج من العهدة بيقين (ويقبل قول
evidence.note: The Iqnāʿ and Kashshāf rule that the certain count is taken, and that the word of two upright witnesses is accepted as in prayer (position 0).

evidence.excerpt_ar: وهو المذهب. اختاره ابن عبدوس في تذكرته. وجزم به في المنور. وقدمه في
evidence.note: al-Inṣāf glosses the Muqniʿ's 'the husband's word with his oath' (in a dispute over the ṣadāq's amount) as the madhhab, chosen by Ibn ʿAbdūs, stated decisively in al-Munawwar and given precedence in al-Muḥarrar and al-Furūʿ: riwāya 1.

evidence.excerpt_ar: الزركشي: اختاره عامة الأصحاب. قال في الفروع: نصره القاضي، وأصحابه. وهو
evidence.note: For the opposing riwāya (the word of whoever claims the fair mahr) al-Inṣāf reports that al-Zarkashī said most of the aṣḥāb chose it and that al-Qāḍī and his followers championed it. This supports position 1 but is not the madhhab.

evidence.excerpt_ar: (صفته أو) في (جنسه أو ما يستقر به) من وطء أو خلوة ونحوهما (فقول زوج)
evidence.note: Kashshāf rules that in a dispute over the amount of the ṣadāq (among other things), the husband's word is taken with his oath (position 0).

evidence.excerpt_ar: وإذا اختلفا أو ورثتهما أو زوج، وولي صغيرة في قدر صداق أو عينه أو صفته
evidence.note: The Muntahā rules that in disputes over the amount of the ṣadāq the husband's (or his heir's) word is taken with his oath, as the next line states (position 0).

evidence.excerpt_ar: قولها. وهو المذهب؛ لأن الظاهر معها. اختاره القاضي. قال في الخلاصة:
evidence.note: al-Inṣāf: the wife's word is the madhhab because the ẓāhir is with her, and al-Mardāwī adds 'qultu: wa-huwa al-ṣawāb', i.e. position 1.

evidence.excerpt_ar: بل سبق أحدنا بالإسلام (ف) القول (قولها) لأن الظاهر معها إذ يبعد اتفاق
evidence.note: Kashshāf rules that the wife's word is taken, since simultaneous conversion is unlikely (position 1).

evidence.excerpt_ar: وإن قال أسلمنا معا فنحن على النكاح فأنكرته فقولها وإن أسلم أحدهما بعد
evidence.note: The Muntahā states decisively that the wife's word is taken (position 1).

entries.note: Ibn Rajab gives the better reason for the second wajh.

evidence.excerpt_ar: أنكر الولي عدم علمه بذلك ولا بينة: قبل قوله مع يمينه. وهو المذهب. اختاره
evidence.note: al-Inṣāf: if the guardian denies knowing of the defect and there is no proof, his word is accepted with his oath, and that is the madhhab (with insanity excepted per al-Riʿāya), i.e. position 0. al-Qāḍī's and Ibn ʿAqīl's distinction between close and distant guardians is listed only as a 'qīla'.

evidence.excerpt_ar: ويرجع به على مغر من زوجة عاقلة وولي ووكيل ويقبل قول ولي ولو محرما في عدم
evidence.note: The Muntahā rules that the guardian's word is accepted even if he is a maḥram (i.e. a close guardian), which rejects position 1.

evidence.excerpt_ar: كأبيها وأخيها وعمها وكذا وكيلها (في عدم علمه به) أي العيب حيث لا بينة
evidence.note: Sharḥ al-Muntahā names the father, brother and uncle explicitly: their denial of knowing the defect is accepted, because the aṣl is ignorance (position 0).

evidence.excerpt_ar: وغيره. وقدمه الأزجي وغيره. قلت: وهو المذهب على ما
evidence.note: al-Inṣāf lists four views on eating from wealth containing ḥarām. It makes the fourth the madhhab per its stated convention: no prohibition however much or little the ḥarām, but karāha that strengthens with the ḥarām's share. This maps to permission (position 0).

evidence.excerpt_ar: ابن عقيل في الفصول وغيره وقدمه الأزجي وغيره قال في الإنصاف: وهذا المذهب
evidence.note: The Iqnāʿ and Kashshāf rule that accepting the invitation of, eating from or dealing with one whose wealth mixes ḥalāl and ḥarām is disliked, not forbidden, citing al-Inṣāf's 'this is the madhhab' (position 0).

evidence.excerpt_ar: والقول الثالث: إن كان الحرام أكثر: حرم الأكل، وإلا فلا. إقامة للأكثر
evidence.note: The third view in al-Inṣāf, forbidding eating when the ḥarām is the majority, was stated decisively by Ibn al-Jawzī in al-Minhāj. It supports position 1 but is not the madhhab.

evidence.excerpt_ar: المصنف، والشارح هنا: أنه يحد، وصححه في الرعايتين، وقدمه في الحاوي. وهو
evidence.note: For a man who accuses an unknown-lineage woman of zinā and claims she is a slave while she denies it, al-Inṣāf says the hadd applies: corrected in al-Riʿāyatayn, given precedence by al-Muṣannif and al-Shāriḥ, and continuing 'wa-huwa al-madhhab'. This is position 1.

evidence.excerpt_ar: (وكذا لو قذف مجهولة النسب وادعى رقها وأنكرته) فيحد وكذا لو قذف مجهول
evidence.note: Kashshāf rules that the accuser receives the hadd, for a male of unknown lineage as for a female (position 1).

evidence.excerpt_ar: لو قذف مجهولة النسب وادعى رقها فأنكرته) فيحد لأن الأصل الحرية (وإن ثبت
evidence.note: The Muntahā and its sharḥ rule the hadd, because the aṣl is freedom (position 1).

evidence.excerpt_ar: بكر، والرواية الأخرى: تطلق واحدة، وهو المذهب، اختاره المصنف، وقال: هو
evidence.note: al-Inṣāf: when no number is intended, 'anti al-ṭalāq' / 'al-ṭalāq yalzamunī' gives one divorce, and that is the madhhab (chosen by al-Muṣannif, stated decisively in al-Wajīz, given precedence in al-Muḥarrar and al-Furūʿ). This is position 0.

evidence.excerpt_ar: معلقا بشرط أو محلوفا به ويقع به واحدة ما لم ينو أكثر فمن معه عدد، وثم
evidence.note: The Muntahā states decisively that one divorce falls unless more is intended (position 0).

evidence.excerpt_ar: (ومع عدمها) أي عدم نية الثلاث بأن نوى واحدة أو أطلق، يقع (واحدة) لأن أهل
evidence.note: Kashshāf: without an intention of three, one divorce falls, because ordinary speakers do not take the article as exhaustive (position 0).

evidence.excerpt_ar: جزم في الكافي، وغيره: بأنه يلزمه ثلاثة مع الإطلاق وقال ابن رزين: يلزمه
evidence.note: al-Inṣāf reports that al-Kāfī and others state decisively that three are owed when the statement is unqualified, with al-Furūʿ and others giving it precedence (position 1).

evidence.excerpt_ar: درهم لزمه ثلاثة) دراهم لأنه مقتضى إقراره (وإن نوى بالثالث تأكيد الثاني
evidence.note: Kashshāf rules that repeating 'a dirham' three times with wa-, fa- or thumma makes three owed, and an intention that the third confirms the second is not accepted where there is a conjunction (position 1).

evidence.excerpt_ar: درهمان وكذا درهم ودرهم فلو كرره ثلاثا بالواو أو الفاء أو ثم أو قال درهم
evidence.note: The Muntahā rules three for a threefold repetition with wa- (with no ta'kīd accepted when there is a conjunction), i.e. position 1.

evidence.excerpt_ar: واحدة، فالصحيح من المذهب: أنه يقرع ms2097 بينهم. قال في الرعاية الصغرى: وإن سبق
evidence.note: For several who reach a public mine too narrow for all, al-Mardāwī labels drawing lots al-ṣaḥīḥ min al-madhhab (also put first in al-Furūʿ and al-Qawāʿid), against the ruler-chooses, division and al-Qāḍī alternatives.

evidence.excerpt_ar: جملة أقرع كطريق) أي كما لو سبق اثنان فأكثر إلى طريق واسع وضاق عن جلوسهما
evidence.note: Kashshāf/Iqnāʿ rule decisively that lots are drawn, by analogy with a road too narrow for both to sit.

evidence.excerpt_ar: فأكثر إليه وضاق المكان عن أخذهم جملة: أقرع كطريق وإن حفره إنسان من جانب
evidence.note: The Iqnāʿ matn states the lot without a dispute.

evidence.excerpt_ar: المذهب. قال الحارثي: والمذهب القرعة، ودفعها إلى القارع مع يمينه. نص
evidence.note: On "if two describe the luqaṭa" al-Mardāwī says the lot-then-oath wajh "wa-huwa al-madhhab", quoting al-Ḥārithī that the madhhab is the lot and that it is manṣūṣ (al-Mardāwī adds "wa-huwa al-ṣawāb").

evidence.excerpt_ar: دفعها إلى الأول أو أقام بينتين - أقرع بينهما فمن قرع حلف وأخذها وبعد
evidence.note: The Iqnāʿ rules decisively that when two describe it together (or the second before handover) lots are drawn and the winner swears and takes it.

evidence.excerpt_ar: منهم في ظاهر كلامه) . هو إحدى الروايتين. ونص عليه في رواية ابن منصور.
evidence.note: On a bequest of an unspecified slave al-Mardāwī says the heirs give whichever they wish, manṣūṣ in the riwāya of Ibn Manṣūr; the next line reads "wa-huwa al-madhhab" and al-Khiraqī's lot is reported as the other riwāya.

evidence.excerpt_ar: تناول واحدا فيلزم الموصى له قبول ما يدفعه الوارث من صحيح أو معيب جيد أو
evidence.note: Kashshāf rules that the heirs give whatever they wish and the legatee must accept even a defective one, since the name covers it, which is the minimum-of-the-name reasoning of the manṣūṣ.

evidence.excerpt_ar: أوصى له بعبد مجهول من عبيده صح ويعطيه الورثة ما شاؤا منهم فأن لم يكن له
evidence.note: The Iqnāʿ matn states decisively that the heirs give him whichever slave they wish.

evidence.excerpt_ar: المذهب: أن حكمها حكم المسألة التي قبلها. وعليه أكثر الأصحاب.
evidence.note: For order known and then forgotten, al-Mardāwī says al-ṣaḥīḥ min al-madhhab is to treat it like the unknown-order case (mutual inheritance from tilād property), held by most aṣḥāb; al-Qawāʿid also calls it the madhhab.

evidence.excerpt_ar: أو جهلوا عينه ولم يختلفوا في السابق ورث كل واحد من الموتى صاحبه من تلاد
evidence.note: The Iqnāʿ includes "ʿulima thumma nusiya" with unknown order and rules decisively for mutual inheritance from tilād property.

evidence.excerpt_ar: لا؟ أو علم ثم نسي، أو جهلوا عينه فإن لم يدع ورثة كل سبق الآخر ورث كل ميت
evidence.note: The Muntahā gives the same decisive ruling for the forgotten order when the heirs do not dispute.

evidence.excerpt_ar: الصحيح من المذهب. نص عليه. قال المصنف هنا: وهذا أحسن إن شاء الله تعالى.
evidence.note: For heirs who dispute the order with no proof, or with conflicting proofs, al-Mardāwī rules "taḥālafā wa-lam yatawārathā ʿalā al-ṣaḥīḥ min al-madhhab, naṣṣ ʿalayh" (the previous line), al-Furūʿ adding that most chose it.

evidence.excerpt_ar: وإن ادعوه ولا بينة أو تعارضتا تحالفا ولم يتوارثا ففي امرأة وابنها
evidence.note: The Muntahā rules decisively that disputing heirs swear and there is no mutual inheritance.

entries.note: Ibn Abī Mūsā's «أظهر وأصح» is his own preference.

evidence.excerpt_ar: الروايتين. وهو المذهب. جزم به الخرقي، وصاحب الوجيز، والمنور، وغيرهم
evidence.note: On "two guardians marry her and the earlier is unknown", al-Mardāwī says the riwāya that both marriages are annulled is al-madhhab, and the annulment is done by the ḥākim (ʿalā al-ṣaḥīḥ); the lot riwāya is chosen by al-Najjād, al-Qāḍī (Taʿlīq), al-Sharīf, Abū al-Khaṭṭāb and al-Shīrāzī.

evidence.excerpt_ar: أن أحدهما قبل الزوال والآخر بعده (وجهل السابق) منهما (فسخهما حاكم) لأن
evidence.note: Kashshāf rules decisively that the ḥākim annuls both when the earlier contract is unknown or forgotten; the lot is used only to fix who owes half the mahr.

evidence.excerpt_ar: أو علم سابق ثم نسي أو علم السبق وجهل السابق فسخهما حاكم فإن علم وقوعهما
evidence.note: The Muntahā states the ḥākim's annulment of both without a dispute.

evidence.excerpt_ar: السابق فسخهما حاكم ولها نصف المهر يقترعان عليه وكذا لو طلقاها وأن أقرت
evidence.note: The Iqnāʿ likewise rules annulment by the ḥākim, with a lot only over the half-mahr.

entries.note: The naṣṣ endorses both lot and the middle one.

evidence.excerpt_ar: المذهب: لها أحدهم بالقرعة. على الصحيح من المذهب. نص عليه في رواية مهنا.
evidence.note: On the madhhab (validity of a dower of "one of his slaves") al-Mardāwī rules she gets one by lot "ʿalā al-ṣaḥīḥ min al-madhhab", manṣūṣ in the riwāya of Muhannā, against "lahā al-wasaṭ" (Ibn ʿAbdūs, al-Muḥarrar) and Ibn ʿAqīl's wujūh.

evidence.excerpt_ar: فيه يسيرة ولها أحدهم بقرعة نصا وأن أصدقها عبدا موصوفا صح فإن جاءها
evidence.note: The Iqnāʿ rules decisively that the dower is valid and she gets one by lot, naṣṣan.

evidence.excerpt_ar: قمصانه ونحوه) كخاتم من خواتمه (صح، ولها أحدهم بقرعة) نصا ; لأن الجهالة
evidence.note: The Muntahā and its sharḥ likewise give her one by lot, since the uncertainty is slight and the lot can fix it.

evidence.excerpt_ar: أحدهما خطأ الآخر، في أصح الوجهين فيهما، نقل ابن القاسم " فليتقيا الشبهة
evidence.note: For the two men's opposite raven oaths al-Mardāwī, quoting al-Furūʿ, rules that neither wife is divorced and intercourse is forbidden to both unless one believes the other wrong, "fī aṣaḥḥ al-wajhayn fīhimā".

evidence.excerpt_ar: الوطء إلا مع اعتقاد أحدهما خطأ الآخر، في الأصح فيهما، نقل ابن القاسم
evidence.note: Ibn Mufliḥ marks as al-aṣaḥḥ that the marriage rules stay in force (no divorce) while both must abstain unless one believes the other mistaken.

evidence.excerpt_ar: تعتقا) أي الأمتان (ولم تطلقا) أي المرأتان، لأن الحانث منهما ليس معلوما
evidence.note: Kashshāf/Iqnāʿ rule decisively that neither wife is divorced, because the one who broke his oath is unknown, with intercourse forbidden to both.

evidence.excerpt_ar: ولم يعلما لم تطلقا ولم تعتقا ويحرم عليهما الوطء إلا مع اعتقاد أحدهما خطأ
evidence.note: The Muntahā states the same: no divorce, but intercourse forbidden unless one believes the other wrong; a lot comes in only if one buys the other's slave-girl.

evidence.excerpt_ar: قوله (وإن تداعيا معا: قدم قولها) ، هذا المذهب، صححه في المغني، والشرح،
evidence.note: When rajʿa and the end of ʿidda are claimed at the same moment, al-Mardāwī says the wife's word prevailing is al-madhhab; the lot is only an iḥtimāl of Abū al-Khaṭṭāb.

evidence.excerpt_ar: أحدها: يؤخذ بقولها، وهو الصحيح، قطع به في الوجيز وغيره، وصححه في
evidence.note: In Taṣḥīḥ al-Furūʿ (masʾala 4) al-Mardāwī corrects the three views Ibn Mufliḥ left unweighted in favour of the wife's word.

evidence.excerpt_ar: فلا يقبل قولها في إبطالها (وإن تداعيا) ذلك (معا قدم قولها) لتساقط قولهما
evidence.note: Kashshāf/Iqnāʿ rule decisively for the wife: the two claims cancel out and the default is no rajʿa.

evidence.excerpt_ar: يوجد قافة) أو اختلف قائفان (ضاع نسبه في أحد الوجهين) . وهو المذهب. نص
evidence.note: When the qāfa fail, are absent or disagree, al-Mardāwī says loss of lineage is al-madhhab (Abū Bakr), against waiting for puberty (Ibn Ḥāmid); the lot is only a riwāya reported from al-Mughnī.

evidence.excerpt_ar: (أو اختلف قائفان أو) اختلف (اثنان وثلاثة فأكثر ضاع نسبه) لعدم المرجح
evidence.note: Kashshāf/Iqnāʿ rule decisively that his lineage is lost when there is no qāfa or they disagree, with no lot.

evidence.excerpt_ar: أو نفته أو أشكل أمره اختلف قائفان أو اثنان وثلاثة ضاع نسبه ويؤخذ باثنين
evidence.note: The Muntahā states the loss of lineage decisively.

evidence.excerpt_ar: (حرم استرقاقهم) على الصحيح من المذهب. نص عليه في رواية ابن هانئ. وعليه
evidence.note: When the musta'man in the fortress cannot be identified, al-Mardāwī rules killing them is forbidden "bilā nizāʿ" and enslaving them is forbidden "ʿalā al-ṣaḥīḥ min al-madhhab", held by most aṣḥāb; Abū Bakr's lot is the other view.

evidence.excerpt_ar: تغليب التحريم، كما لو اشتبه زان محصن بمعصومين (و) حرم (استرقاقهم) ؛ لأن
evidence.note: Kashshāf rules decisively that killing and enslaving them are forbidden, giving priority to prohibition.

evidence.excerpt_ar: ومن أسلم أو أعطى أمانا ليفتح حصنا ففتحه واشتبه وادعوه حرم قتلهم ورقهم
evidence.note: The Muntahā states decisively that killing and enslaving them are forbidden.

evidence.excerpt_ar: انتهى. قلت: فالمذهب المنصوص: أنه لا يلزمه شيء، قال في الفروع: وحكي عن
evidence.note: Having reported al-Qawāʿid's survey, al-Mardāwī concludes that the madhhab, manṣūṣ, is that nothing is binding on one who swore an oath of unknown kind.

evidence.excerpt_ar: انتهى. قلت: والنفس تميل إلى القرعة، لأن ذمته قد اشتغلت قطعا إما بطلاق أو
evidence.note: In Taṣḥīḥ al-Furūʿ (masʾala 6) al-Mardāwī says he inclines to the lot, since his liability is certainly engaged by a divorce or a ẓihār; this is a personal ikhtiyār, not a taṣḥīḥ of the madhhab.

entries.note: Both are al-Qāḍī's takhrīj from the two-guardians case.

evidence.excerpt_ar: لهما معا أو جهل السابق منهما فالعقد باطل فيهما) لأن العمل ببيعة أحدهما
evidence.note: Kashshāf rules decisively that if allegiance was given to two and the earlier is unknown, the contract is void for both, since acting on either would be preference without a ground.

evidence.excerpt_ar: بويع لهما معا أو جهل السابق منهما فالعقد باطل فيهما ويجبر متعين لها
evidence.note: The Iqnāʿ matn states the voidness of both contracts without a dispute.

evidence.excerpt_ar: كل منهما أنه لا حق له للآخر فيها (وتناصفاها) أي قسمت بينهما لاستوائهما،
evidence.note: The Muntahā and its sharḥ rule that a thing in no one's hand, with no evidence and no proof, is shared: both swear and it is halved.

evidence.excerpt_ar: لو لم تكن بيد أحد: فنقل صالح، وحنبل: هي لأحدهما بقرعة، كالتي بيد ثالث.
evidence.note: Al-Inṣāf reports that Ḥanbal as well as Ṣāliḥ transmitted the lot for a thing in no one's hand, and that al-Furūʿ puts it first; the Ḥanbal transmission is not among the listed holders.

evidence.excerpt_ar: (وإن لم تكن) العين (بيد أحد) وتنازعها اثنان (فهي لأحدهما بقرعة) نص
evidence.note: Kashshāf rules for the lot, citing the naṣṣ of Ṣāliḥ and Ḥanbal and al-Furūʿ's taqdīm, while noting that he gave halving earlier in the chapter.

evidence.excerpt_ar: لهما. فيسقطان بالتعارض. وهذه الرواية هي المذهب. وجزم به في العمدة.
evidence.note: For a thing in both their hands with equal conflicting proofs, al-Mardāwī says the riwāya that the proofs fall away and the parties swear as if there were no proof is al-madhhab, against the division-without-oath riwāya (corrected in al-Mughnī and al-Sharḥ) and the lot riwāya (Ṣāliḥ).

evidence.excerpt_ar: تعارضتا وتساقطتا فيتحالفان ويتناصفان ما بأيديهما ويقرع فيما ليس بيد أحد
evidence.note: The Muntahā rules decisively that equal proofs conflict and fall away; then the parties swear and halve what is in their hands, with a lot for what is in no one's hand or a third party's.
